The field numbers above are part of the committed wire contract and must not be renumbered. `at_ms`
is an epoch-millisecond integer; it is never formatted with a locale or timezone. The JavaScript
objects used by the clients keep the REST shape `{ siteId, watts, atMs }`.

> **Released-contract note:** the comment on `StreamReadings` in `proto/energy.proto` still describes
> the first release, where an omitted or zero limit returned an empty stream. The released protocol
> file is deliberately kept byte-for-byte unchanged. The effective behaviour is the Fleet
> compatibility correction dated 2026-11-10: an omitted or zero limit selects the first three
> available readings in source order (see "Fleet compatibility correction" below).

## Fleet compatibility correction (2026-11-10)

The dated Fleet notice is `updates/2026-11-10/fleet-default-limit.md`. The Fleet consumer uses a
zero or omitted `StreamReadings` limit to request the first three available readings in source
order; the first release incorrectly returned an empty stream for those requests.

The server now applies a default limit of `3` when the decoded limit is zero (which also covers an
omitted field), then takes the same `readings.slice(0, limit)` path as an explicit positive limit.
Positive limits, `GetReading`, unknown-site errors, protobuf field numbers, and REST behaviour are
unchanged from the first release. A site with fewer than three readings returns all of its readings.

args.new_string:
- Request: exactly one `StreamReadingsRequest` frame.
- Response: one `Reading` frame per selected reading, in the same source order as the REST list.
- A positive `limit` selects `readings.slice(0, limit)`.
- An **omitted limit** and an **explicitly zero limit** both use the Fleet default of `3`: they
  return the first three available readings in source order. A site with fewer than three readings
  returns all of them. They do not mean "all readings".
args.old_string:
- Request: exactly one `StreamReadingsRequest` frame.
- Response: one `Reading` frame per selected reading, in the same source order as the REST list.
- `limit` selects `readings.slice(0, limit)`.
- An **omitted limit** and an **explicitly zero limit** both return an empty stream: no Reading
  frames, followed by `grpc-status: 0`. They do not mean "all readings".

`test/integration.test.js` runs the real server through `service/grpc_client.js`, covers omitted/zero
